verdict.headline: Stocks steady as oil tumbles on push to restart US-Iran peace talks
verdict.label: Cautious — oil diplomacy eases the setup; FOMC + Mag-7 capex verdict July 29 is the clearing event
verdict.rationale_short: Oil fell 3-4% (WTI $89.31, Brent $96.78) on a CNBC report that Pakistan and China are brokering new US-Iran talks — the first concrete diplomatic signal of the conflict phase — easing August CPI pressure and pulling VIX to 17.96 from Thursday's 19.38. SPX held 7,411.98 above the 7,380 BEARISH threshold; Dow outperformed (+235 pts on AAPL +3.5%) while Nasdaq lagged (-0.64%) as INTC reversed its full +12% earnings pop to close down 7.89% at $92.32 on foundry external-demand scrutiny. No directional call is appropriate before FOMC July 29 (Chair Warsh press conference 2:30pm ET) and META/MSFT reports the same evening; the oil diplomacy signal is a process, not a ceasefire, and could reverse on any Trump escalation or failed negotiation.

dont_buy.reason: The foundry external-demand concern that triggered Friday's -7.89% reversal to $92.32 is not a one-session reaction. Only Apple and Microsoft were named as 18A external customers on Thursday's call; third-party external revenue remains limited and the foundry model requires multi-customer validation to support its premium valuation. The morning brief's stop at $105 was violated by $12.68. Re-entering after a stop-out into the same thesis within the same week requires a meaningfully higher bar of confirmation.
dont_buy.better_entry: Post-Q3 2026 earnings if external foundry bookings demonstrate customer diversification beyond Apple and Microsoft; or if 18A yield data confirms volume production economics ahead of schedule at lower cost than TSMC 2nm.

dont_buy.reason: Kimi K3's 2.8T parameter open-weight release on Monday creates binary weekend risk. INTC's -7.89% reversal demonstrates that the market will sell AI infrastructure names on business-model concerns even when demand beats expectations — a pattern repeated twice now (GOOGL -7% on capex, INTC -8% on foundry demand). NVDA faces four overlapping risk events in nine trading sessions: Kimi K3 (Monday), FOMC (July 29), three Mag-7 capex reports (July 29-30), and then NVDA Q2 FY27 (August 26).
dont_buy.better_entry: Post-NVDA Q2 FY27 (August 26, est.) with confirmed data-center revenue growth against explicit AMD hyperscaler share commentary; or $188-193 on capitulation with VIX closing below 15 for two consecutive sessions.

dont_buy.reason: Four consecutive losing sessions (-14.52% Thursday, -2.1% Friday) since the Q2 gross-margin miss. At $312.84, TSLA is below every prior capitulation-entry target this briefing series has identified. The structural thesis for Q3 recovery — gross margin above 18%, FCF positive — requires at least two quarters of validation. Oil's WTI retreat to $89 provides marginal EV fuel-cost tailwind but does not address the pricing-versus-cost operating-leverage problem.
dont_buy.better_entry: $295-310 if SPX tests the 7,380 BEARISH threshold post-FOMC and institutional forced-selling completes; or post-Q3 earnings (late October) if gross margin recovers above 18% and FCF turns positive.

trade_setups.thesis: Brent crude fell to $96.78 on the Pakistan-China diplomatic signal for US-Iran talks — a meaningful risk reduction but not a ceasefire. August CPI oil pass-through is partially reduced (Brent below $100) but not eliminated (WTI $89.31 is still $10.31 above the $79 trigger). Trimming from 20% to 12-15% preserves the upside if oil spikes back on talks failure while reducing exposure to a further retreat if diplomatic progress accelerates toward a ceasefire framework.
trade_setups.entry: Reduce from 20% to 12-15% at Friday close or Monday open. Add back to 20% if Brent re-crosses $100 on confirmed talks failure or Trump escalation. Reduce further to 8% only on Iran-US ceasefire formally announced AND Hormuz transit above 10 vessels/day AND WTI two consecutive closes below $70.
trade_setups.invalidation: Iran-US formal ceasefire announced with Hormuz reopening confirmed; WTI two consecutive closes below $70.

trade_setups.thesis: September hike probability remains approximately 74% (est.) even after oil's Friday retreat — still above the 70% regime-breach trigger. FOMC Chair Warsh's July 29 press conference is the session where rate language either closes or extends the September window. META and MSFT report the same evening, creating the single highest-density day of the year for rate + capex risk. The IWM/TLT hedge must not be unwound before both the FOMC statement and all three Mag-7 July 29-30 prints have cleared.
trade_setups.entry: Maintain IWM August puts at full original size. Maintain TLT short above $87.50. Reassess AFTER FOMC July 29 decision AND META/MSFT July 29 AH prints — both must clear before re-evaluating size.
trade_setups.invalidation: FOMC explicitly closes September door (September hike probability falls below 55%) AND Brent holds below $90 for three sessions AND META/MSFT both beat on AI capex ROI improving quarter-over-quarter. All three simultaneously required.
trade_setups.horizon: Through FOMC July 28-29 and August CPI (est. Aug 13)

trade_setups.thesis: Kimi K3's 2.8T parameter open-weight model release on Monday July 27 is the cleanest downside binary for NVDA heading into the weekend — Moonshot AI's model offers approximately 70% inference pricing discount vs. API providers, directly challenging hyperscaler inference capex ROI. INTC's -7.89% reversal on foundry external-demand concerns demonstrates that the market will sell AI infrastructure names on business-model questions even when demand beats consensus — a pattern now confirmed twice (GOOGL -7%, INTC -8%). NVDA at $206.66 faces a four-event dead zone in nine sessions, none of which is unambiguously positive.
trade_setups.entry: Short NVDA at $204-208. Stop above $216 (prior week's high; short-squeeze resistance level). Target $190-196. Half a standard position given NVDA's volatility and short-squeeze potential on a FOMC-dovish relief rally.
trade_setups.invalidation: Kimi K3 releases below benchmark performance on a key dimension (removing the inference-efficiency narrative); FOMC is explicitly dovish with September closed; NVDA pre-announces strong Q2 FY27 datacenter demand ahead of August 26.
trade_setups.horizon: Through Kimi K3 (Jul 27) and FOMC (Jul 29); reassess after both events

bear_case: The Pakistan-China diplomatic push for US-Iran talks is a soft signal from a mediating third party with limited coercive leverage over either Washington or Tehran — Trump's 'major military punishment' threat for future Hormuz attacks was not withdrawn on Friday, and Brent at $96.78 remains $12 above the $85 regime trigger and $7 above the $90 level that sustains the August CPI oil pass-through thesis. INTC's -7.89% reversal despite the largest revenue beat of the quarter demonstrates a pattern the briefing series has now confirmed twice: the market will reprice AI infrastructure names aggressively on business-model scrutiny even when top-line demand is strong (GOOGL -7% on capex, INTC -8% on foundry external demand); META and MSFT report into this exact framework on July 29. If Chair Warsh's FOMC statement acknowledges that tariff-on-99.4%-of-imports is not transitory, September hike probability re-prices above 80%, immediately reversing the oil dip's rate-relief benefit. Bear case invalidation: Iran formally agrees to ceasefire framework talks (formal agreement, not diplomatic signals) AND Brent holds below $90 for two consecutive sessions AND FOMC July 29 statement explicitly removes September from the base case (probability falls below 55%). All three simultaneously required.
